modules.title: Introduction to Number Systems and Logic
modules.html:
Binary, octal and hexadecimal numbers, conversions and logic gates. This section covers introduction to number systems and logic.

Key points

  • The binary equivalent of the decimal number 10 is _____. — 1010.
  • Which logic gate produces an output of 1 only when all its inputs are 1 — AND gate.
  • The hexadecimal number system uses base _____. — 16.
  • Convert the binary number 111 to decimal. — 7.
  • The base of the Octal number system is _____. — 8.

Worked examples

Q: The binary equivalent of the decimal number 10 is _____.
A: 1010 — To convert 10 to binary: 10/2 = 5 R 0; 5/2 = 2 R 1; 2/2 = 1 R 0; 1/2 = 0 R 1. Reading remainders from bottom to top gives 1010.

Q: Which logic gate produces an output of 1 only when all its inputs are 1?
A: AND gate — In an AND gate, the output is high (1) if and only if all the input signals are high (1).

examples.q: The binary equivalent of the decimal number 10 is _____.
Which logic gate produces an output of 1 only when all its inputs are 1?

quiz.solution: In an AND gate, the output is high (1) if and only if all the input signals are high (1).

quiz.q: The hexadecimal number system uses base _____.
quiz.solution: Hexadecimal uses sixteen distinct symbols: 0–9 and A–F.

quiz.q: Convert the binary number 111 to decimal.
The base of the Octal number system is _____.
quiz.solution: Octal uses eight digits: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, and 7.

quiz.q: Which logic gate is also known as an 'Inverter'?
quiz.solution: A NOT gate is called an inverter because it reverses the input signal (1 becomes 0 and vice versa).

quiz.q: Which logic gate outputs 1 only if both inputs are 1?

quiz.q: Which Logic Gate inverts input?
